'''Ottis Jerome Anderson''' (born January 19, 1957) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 14 seasons with the [[St. Louis Cardinals (NFL)|St. Louis Cardinals]] and [[New York Giants]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]], setting the school record for rushing yards, and was selected eighth overall in the [[1979 NFL draft]] by the Cardinals.

In his first season, Anderson was named [[NFL Rookie of the Year Award|Offensive Rookie of the Year]] and received [[Pro Bowl]] and first-team [[All-Pro]] honors when he set the Cardinals all-time record for rushing yards. He also received a second Pro Bowl selection the following year. Traded to the Giants in 1986 amid a production decline, Anderson won two [[Super Bowl]] titles in [[Super Bowl XXI]] and [[Super Bowl XXV]]. Anderson was named [[Super Bowl Most Valuable Player award|MVP]] of the latter, in which he played a central part in helping the Giants set the Super Bowl record for time of possession.

'''Ozzie Newsome Jr.''' (born March 16, 1956) is an American professional [[American football|football]] executive and former player who is the executive vice president of player personnel of the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Newsome was a [[tight end]] for the NFL's [[Cleveland Browns]], and was general manager of the Ravens from 1996 to 2018. Newsome has been inducted into both the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] (1994) and the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] (1999).

'''Ositadimma''' "'''Osi'''" '''Umenyiora''' ({{IPAc-en||audio=Ig-Ositadimma "Osi" Umenyiora.ogg}}; born November 16, 1981) is a British-Nigerian former professional [[American football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Troy Trojans football|Troy Trojans]] and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the second round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. With the Giants, he won [[Super Bowl XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI]], both over the [[New England Patriots]]. Umenyiora was a two-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection and holds the Giants franchise record for most sacks in one game. He is one of five British-born players to have won a [[Super Bowl]], joining [[Marvin Allen (wide receiver)|Marvin Allen]], [[Scott McCready]], former Troy and Giants teammate [[Lawrence Tynes]],<ref name="british">{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Ralston |author2=Mcdonald, Craig |title=Delight Of Super Bowl Hero Scot Lawrence Tynes |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/editors-choice/2008/02/05/delight-of-super-bowl-hero-scot-lawrence-tynes-86908-20309544/ |work=Daily Record |date=February 5, 2008 }}</ref> and [[Jay Ajayi]]. He also played for the [[Atlanta Falcons]].

'''Ove Claes Johansson''' (March 31, 1948 – September 30, 2023) was a Swedish American [[American football|football]] [[placekicker]] who kicked what was then the longest [[Field goal (football)|field goal]] in the sport's history at {{convert|69|yd|m}} in 1976.<ref name="deadspin">{{cite web|url=http://deadspin.com/5955305/an-interview-with-ove-johansson-the-man-who-kicked-the-longest-field-goal-ever|title=An Interview With Ove Johansson, The Man Who Kicked The Longest Field Goal Ever|last=Dickey|first=Jack|date=26 October 2012|access-date=12 July 2017|publisher=Deadspin.com}}</ref> Johansson is the oldest player to be drafted in the [[National Football League Draft|NFL draft]], being 28 years, 281 days old when he was selected in the 12th round of the [[1977 NFL draft]] by the [[History of the Tennessee Titans|Houston Oilers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/photos/0ap1000000145639/0ap2000000154745|title=Countdown to the 2013 NFL Draft|work=[[National Football League]]|access-date=April 2, 2013}}</ref>

Johansson was a junior at [[Abilene Christian University]] after being an all American soccer player at national power [[Davis and Elkins College]], and performed this kick during ACU's 1976 [[homecoming]] game against [[Texas A&M University-Commerce|East Texas State University]] at [[Shotwell Stadium]], in [[Abilene, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://naia.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/091205aaf.html |title=[[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics{{!}}NAIA]] Football Records :: Individual and Team game, season and career<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-12-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928224410/http://naia.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/091205aaf.html |archive-date=2011-09-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.nflhs.com/news/features/Legends_DirkBorgognone%20_11282005_lcb.asp NFLHS.COM -
